sentences.text: A.Padmavathi, vs D.Appa Rao, on 15 February, 2024

Author: N. Tukaramji
Bench: P.Sam Koshy, N.Tukaramji
 Honourable Sri Justice P. Sam Koshy
 And
 Honourable Sri Justice N. Tukaramji
 M.A.C.M.A. No.1124 of 2016
Judgment:

(per Hon'ble Sri Justice N. Tukaramji) We have heard Mr. I. Gopal Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr. Kota Subba Rao, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurer and perused the record.

2. This appeal is directed against the decree and order dated 26.10.2015 in M.V.O.P.No.492 of 2010 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Secunderabad.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.75 lakhs for the death of Mr. ARV Krishnam Raju in an automobile accident.

4. The appellants/petitioners (hereinafter 'the petitioners') case in brief is that, on 30.04.2010 at 3.15 p.m. at Panjagutta NTR,J 2 MACMA_1124_2016 flyover while ARV Ramakrishna/deceased who is husband and father of petitioners 1 and 2 respectively proceeding on his Hero Honda Shine motorcycle bearing registration No.AP28AX 1611, another motorcycle i.e. Hero Honda CD Dawn bearing registration No. AP-7 AA 8366 (hereinafter 'the crime vehicle') driven by its rider in rash and negligent manner struck the motorcycle of the deceased and caused severe injuries all over his body and while undergoing treatment in Yashoda Hospital succumbed to injuries.

Further pleaded that the deceased was aged 49 years and earned Rs.50,589/- per month as Technical Assistant in BHEL and the death had caused loss of their dependency, prayed for grant of Rs.75 lakhs as compensation.
5. During trial
the first petitioner got herself examined as PW-1, the eyewitness as PW-2 and the Officer in Human Resources of BHEL as PW-3 and marked Exs:A-1 to A-8 and X- 1 to X-9.
The respondent No.3/insurer got examined its officer/RW-1, the investigating officer/Ravi Kumar/RW-2 and treating doctors/RWs.3 and 4 and marked Exs:B-1 and C-1.

The tribunal basing on the evidence of the eyewitness/PW-2 and the investigating officer/RW-2,
held that the discrepancies in the versions of the eyewitness and non filing of motor vehicle A.Padmavathi, vs D.Appa Rao, on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110483899/
1 inspector's report to prove the involvement of the crime vehicle and the evidence of RWs.3 and 4 are falling short in establishing the nexus between the injuries suffered in the accident and the death,
dismissed the petition.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the evidence of eyewitness/PW-2 and the investigating officer/RW- 2 are establishing the involvement of crime vehicle in the accident and the medical evidence is showing that while undergoing treatment the deceased succumbed.
Thus the tribunal erred in concluding that the crime vehicle was not involved in the accident and the death was not due to the injuries suffered in the accident.
Thus prayed for interference.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/insurer would submit that the statement of PW-2 itself making out the improbability of being eyewitness to the occurrence.
Further the NTR,J 4 MACMA_1124_2016 first information statement about the accident was after 22 days and no material has been referred as to how the involvement of the crime vehicle was made out.

Above all,
it is for the petitioners to prove that the injuries suffered in the accident led to the death.
In absence of evidence, the tribunal had rightly dismissed the petition and there no tenable ground to consider otherwise in the appeal.
9. We have carefully considered the submissions and perused the materials on record.
10. At the outset the date of the accident, the deceased's admission in the hospital undergoing treatment, later his death are not specifically disputed by the respondent No.3/insurer.

11. The tribunal had rejected the claim petition on two grounds; firstly the involvement of the crime vehicle has not been established secondly, the evidence is failing to prove that the death of the deceased was consequence of the injuries suffered in the accident.
In regard to accident and involvement of the crime vehicle, the petitioners relied on the evidence of eyewitness/ PW-2 and the final report/Ex.A-2 of the investigating agency.

13. The eyewitness/PW-2 in his chief examination affidavit supported the petitioners' version and stated that when he reached Green Lands Cross roads, the crime vehicle driven in rash and negligent manner dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.
In cross examination admitted that he did not lodge police report about the accident.
But asserted that he got admitted the injured in the hospital and the crime vehicle crossed his scooter and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.

In cross examination stated that, he did not observe whether the accused was riding the motorcycle and there was any pillion rider and even added that, he cannot identity the person on the crime vehicle and there may be another pillion rider on the crime vehicle and he does not remember the name of hospital in which he got joined the injured/deceased.

2 14.

The investigating officer/RW-2 deposed that the statement of the deceased was recorded on 22.05.2010 and on receipt of information of the death on 24.05.2010, section of law was altered and as per the statement of the eyewitnesses he traced the crime vehicle and on examination of its owner he handed over the vehicle and the accused.
Thus filed the charge sheet.

15. A careful analysis of the material on record with the above read evidence is elucidating that in the first information statement, the deceased had stated before police that, his motorcycle was struck by one unknown vehicle.

As per the charge sheet/Ex.A-2 the accident occurred at Panjagutta Flyover,
Panjagutta.
Whereas the statement of the eyewitness/PW-2 is that the accident occurred at Greenlands cross roads.
Thus foundational fact as to place of occurrence is at variance between the police and the eyewitness and this aspect touching the root.

16. Further the PW-2/eyewitness who was not able to give the registration number of his own scooter or the motorcycle of the NTR,J 7 MACMA_1124_2016 deceased but specifies the registration number of the crime vehicle which is another improbability.
17. The inability to give the name of the hospital in which he got admitted the injured/deceased is another doubtful aspect.
18. In addition as per the investigating officer the crime vehicle was traced basing on the information given by the eyewitness.
To note, the complainant was the deceased himself.

As per the investigating officer's account, he secured the presence of the eyewitnesses who includes PW-2 and on their statements he has collected ownership particulars but nothing has been stated as to how the eyewitnesses were identified.

19. A cumulative reading of above noted facts and circumstances especially the statement of eyewitness who was unable to give preliminary detail of his vehicle number and the discrepancy as to the place of occurrence and the deficiencies in the investigating officer's evidence are giving scope to entertain serious doubts as to involvement of the crime vehicle in the NTR,J 8 MACMA_1124_2016 accident.
In this factual position, we find no error of jurisdiction in the conclusions drawn by the tribunal in the impugned order.
20. Thus, in the absence of any merit, the appeal is liable to be and is accordingly dismissed.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions if any, stands closed.
